title: Cubical-distance conjecture for largest minors
statement:
Let $\mathcal{J}\subset {[n]\choose k}$ be an arrangement of largest minors, and let $W\in {[n]\choose k}$. Say that $W$ is $(\geq t,\mathcal{J})$-largest if, for every arrangement of minors ending at $\mathcal{J}$, it is absent from the final $t-1$ arrangements. For a maximal arrangement $\mathcal{J}$ of largest minors and $W\notin\mathcal{J}$, let $cube_d(W,\mathcal{J})$ denote their cubical distance. **Cubical-distance conjecture.** If

$$
cube_d(W,\mathcal{J})=t,
$$

then $W$ is $(\geq t+1,\mathcal{J})$-largest minor. This conjecture predicts that cubical distance from a maximal arrangement controls how far below the largest minors an omitted minor lies. Its resolution is not indicated in the supplied text.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.02600

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of September 2015). “This conjecture was proved independently in and in .”
